info.title: Anjal API
info.description:
Anjal is a multi-tenant email API for AI agents.

Create inboxes on the default `@send.anjal.app` domain or your own custom
domains, send and receive mail, manage drafts, subscribe to real-time
events over WebSocket, and isolate resources across workspaces so your
reseller customers can serve their own end-customers under a single
billing relationship.

Install the TypeScript SDK: `npm install anjal`
([npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/anjal))

MCP server for Claude Desktop / Cursor: `npx -y anjal-mcp`
([npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/anjal-mcp))

## Authentication

Every request is authenticated with the `X-API-Key` header (or
`Authorization: Bearer <key>`). Four key prefixes, each with increasing
scope:

| Prefix   | Scope                                   | Use it for                              |
|----------|-----------------------------------------|-----------------------------------------|
| `sa_...` | Super admin                             | Tenant lifecycle (platform operator)    |
| `tk_...` | Tenant master                           | Everything in your tenant across workspaces |
| `wk_...` | Workspace master                        | One workspace only                      |
| `ak_...` | Inbox (agent) scoped                    | One inbox — its messages, drafts, lists |

## Resource hierarchy

```
Tenant (billing root)
└── Workspace  (isolation container)
    ├── Inboxes
    │   ├── Messages / Threads / Attachments
    │   ├── Drafts
    │   └── Lists
    └── Domains
```

## Sending mail

Mail is sent via `POST /v1/inboxes/{id}/send`. Replies go through
`/reply/{messageId}`, reply-all through `/reply-all/{messageId}`, and
forwards through `/forward/{messageId}`. The `From` header always uses
the inbox's **primary alias** — add a custom-domain address with
`POST /v1/inboxes/{id}/addresses` to change it.

### Safe retries (Idempotency-Key)

Every send endpoint (`/send`, `/reply`, `/reply-all`, `/forward` and
`POST /v1/inboxes/{id}/drafts/{did}/send`) accepts an `Idempotency-Key`
header. Send a unique value (a UUID works) and retry freely: the first
request sends and stores its response; a retry with the same key and the
identical request returns that stored response with the header
`Idempotent-Replayed: true` and sends nothing.

| Situation | Result |
|---|---|
| Same key, different request (body, inbox or endpoint) | `409 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` |
| Same key while the first request is still running | `409 IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` |
| Header present but blank, or longer than 255 characters | `400 IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID` |
| The first send failed (non-2xx) | The key is freed; retry with the same key |

Keys are scoped to your account and expire after 24 hours.

### Labels, open tracking, scheduled send

- **Labels**: pass `labels` (array, or a comma-separated string) on any
  send, reply, reply-all, forward or draft. Change them later with
  `PATCH /v1/inboxes/{id}/messages/{messageId}` or
  `PATCH /v1/inboxes/{id}/threads/{threadId}`, and filter lists with
  `?labels=a,b`. Labels are stored lowercase and deduplicated; at most 32
  per message, each at most 64 characters, no commas.
- **Open tracking**: `trackOpens: true` on a send with an HTML body adds a
  1x1 pixel (the stored copy never contains it). The first open fires
  `message.opened`. Opens are a hint, not proof: Apple Mail Privacy
  Protection fetches images on delivery, and clients that block images
  never report an open.
- **Scheduled send**: set `sendAt` on a draft and Anjal sends it at that
  time. See the Drafts endpoints.
- **Delivery status**: sent messages carry `deliveryStatus`
  (`delivered`, `bounced`, `complained` or `rejected`; null until known)
  and `deliveredAt`.

## Receiving mail

Inbound mail arrives via SMTP on the default domain or any verified
custom domain. Subscribe to delivery events either by registering a
webhook (`POST /v1/webhooks`) or by opening a WebSocket
(`wss://anjal.app/v1/ws`) — useful for in-line 2FA flows where
the agent doesn't have a public webhook receiver.

delete.description: Cascades to all inboxes, domains, and scoped keys. Cannot delete the tenant's default workspace.

post.summary: Create an inbox (idempotent on requested username)
post.description:
Requires tenant master or workspace master key.

## Username allocation
- If `username` is set and your tenant **already** has an inbox at
  `username@domain`, returns that inbox (HTTP **200**, body
  contains `existed: true`). The call is idempotent — safe to
  retry.
- Otherwise tries to create `username@domain`. If the global
  username is taken by another tenant, falls back to
  `username1`, `username2`, … through `username99`. The actual
  allocated username is in the response body.
- Pass `?strict=true` to disable auto-fallback. With strict mode,
  a global collision returns HTTP **409** with the conflicting
  resource info instead of suffixing.

IMAP/SMTP credentials — `apiKey` and `imapPassword` — are only
returned on first creation, never on idempotent returns.

parameters.name: strict
parameters.description:
When `true`, the request fails with `409 USERNAME_TAKEN` if
the requested `username@domain` is already taken by another
tenant. When omitted (default), we auto-fallback to
`username1`, `username2`, etc.

username.description:
Lowercase alphanumeric + `.-_`. Auto-generated from
the tenant name if omitted. **No tenant-id suffix is
appended** — collisions are resolved via sequential
numeric fallback (e.g. `scout`, `scout1`, `scout2`).

workspaceId.description: (Tenant master only) target workspace. Defaults to the tenant's default workspace.

200.description:
Idempotent return — your tenant already has an inbox at the
requested `username@domain`. `existed: true` is set on the
body. `apiKey` and `imapPassword` are NOT re-issued.

201.description: Newly created. `apiKey` and `imapPassword` are returned once — store them now.

409.description:
`USERNAME_TAKEN` — only returned when `?strict=true` is set
and `username@domain` is taken globally. Body includes
`requestedUsername`, `attemptedUsername`, and `domain` for
single-round-trip recovery. Default behavior auto-falls
back without ever returning 409.

parameters.name: workspace
parameters.description: Tenant master only — filter to a single workspace.

get.description: Returns the inbox detail including IMAP/SMTP credentials and the full address list.

patch.summary: Update inbox display name or metadata
patch.description: Username, domain, and canonical identity are immutable. Use `POST /v1/inboxes/{id}/addresses` to change the outbound From.

delete.description: Soft-deletes the inbox, hard-deletes its alias rows, and removes the Stalwart principal. Prior threads and messages are preserved but hidden from listings.

post.description: Attach another accepted address to this inbox. If `primary: true` (the default), it also becomes the outbound `From`. The domain must be either the default domain or a custom domain registered + verified to the same workspace.

parameters.name: address
parameters.description: URL-encoded alias email

delete.description: Cannot remove the canonical (initial) address. If the removed alias was primary, the canonical address becomes primary again.

post.description:
Sends from this inbox. The `From` header is derived from the inbox's primary alias. Pass `verified: true` when you've validated the recipient domain out-of-band (e.g. via verify-email); otherwise, sends to an address that has never replied to this inbox are rejected as a deliverability safeguard.

Pass an `Idempotency-Key` header so a retry never sends twice. `labels` tags the sent message; `trackOpens: true` adds an open-tracking pixel to the HTML body. The `message.sent` webhook payload includes `labels`.

403.description: Inbox paused or plan limit reached

trackOpens.description: Add an open-tracking pixel (HTML body only). See `SendExtras`.

post.description: Sends to the original sender plus every address in the original To list, with any of this inbox's own addresses filtered out.

cc.description: Extra Cc recipient(s) on top of the auto-derived reply-all recipients.

trackOpens.description: Add an open-tracking pixel (HTML body only). See `SendExtras`.

post.description: Prepends a "Forwarded message" header block and sends the combined body.

trackOpens.description: Add an open-tracking pixel (HTML body only). See `SendExtras`.

get.description:
Newest first, each with its `labels`. `?labels=a,b` returns threads
that carry every label across their messages. Spam is left out unless
`includeSpam=true`; a thread containing spam then carries `hasSpam: true`.

get.summary: Get a thread with all messages

parameters.name: view
parameters.description:
Payload weight. `metadata` = no bodies; `snippet` = 200-char plain
snippet; `full` (default) = plainBody only; `raw` = plainBody +
htmlBody. htmlBody is ~95% of a thread's bytes — only request it
when you actually need rendered HTML.

patch.description:
Applies to every message in the thread: labels (replace with `labels`,
or change with `addLabels` / `removeLabels`), read, starred, archived
and spam. Labelling a thread labels each of its messages.

isSpam.description: true moves the thread to Spam; false recovers it.

delete.description: Soft-deletes every message in the thread (moves them to Trash), the same way deleting one message does.

get.description:
One list across every inbox the key can see (tenant, workspace, inbox or
teammate scope). `?labels=a,b` returns messages carrying every label;
with `group=thread` it matches whole threads (a thread matches when any
of its messages carries the labels) and each row carries the thread's
`labels`.

parameters.name: group
parameters.description: `thread` returns one row per thread (its latest message).

get.description: Every label in use, with how many threads carry it. Same scoping as `GET /v1/messages`.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: Limit to one inbox.

get.description:
Full-text search across every inbox the key can see (tenant-, workspace-,
or inbox-scoped automatically by key tier). Matches subject, plain-text
body, and participant addresses. Returns lightweight hits — ids,
participants, subject, receivedAt, hasAttachments, and a ~200-character
snippet centred on the match — never htmlBody, so results stay small
enough for an agent to consume in one call, then fetch the winning
message/thread in full.

parameters.name: query
parameters.description: Full-text across subject, body, and participants.

parameters.name: inboxId
parameters.description: Scope to one inbox. Omit = all inboxes the key can see.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Filter by sender address or domain (substring match).

parameters.name: participant
parameters.description: Match from OR to OR cc (address or domain).

parameters.name: attachmentFilename
parameters.description: Match an attachment filename substring (e.g. `invoice`).

snippet.description: ~200 chars of plain body centred on the match.

get.description:
Lists messages in an inbox. Tracking fields (firstOpenedAt,
openCount, firstClickedAt, clickCount, etc.) are returned on every
row — no separate detail fetch needed for an engagement-aware view.
Each row also carries a ~200-char plain-body `snippet` for triage
without fetching the full message. Filters can be combined.

Every row carries `labels`, `isSpam` and, for sent mail,
`deliveryStatus` and `deliveredAt`. Spam is left out unless
`includeSpam=true`.

parameters.name: opened
parameters.description: When true, return only messages with open_count > 0.

parameters.name: clicked
parameters.description:
When true, return only messages with click_count > 0. Useful for
cadence engines listing engaged leads who haven't yet replied.

parameters.name: engagedSince
parameters.description:
ISO-8601 timestamp. Returns only messages whose lastOpenedAt OR
lastClickedAt is at or after this time. Use for incremental
polling — pass the timestamp of your last successful sync.

get.description:
Returns full bodies plus attachment metadata. Also marks the message as read.

Some mail clients paste a screenshot straight into the HTML as a `data:`
URI, which can be hundreds of KB inside `htmlBody`. Pass
`inlineImages=refs` to get each one replaced by `attachment:<id>`, the
id of the attachment holding the same image, and that attachment marked
`inline: true`. Fetch it from the attachments endpoint. The response then
also carries `inlineImages: { replaced, unmatched }`; `unmatched` counts
images that had no matching attachment and were removed with no pointer.
Without the parameter `htmlBody` is returned exactly as received.

parameters.name: inlineImages
parameters.description: `refs` replaces inline `data:` images in `htmlBody` with `attachment:<id>` references.

patch.description:
Change labels (replace with `labels`, or change with `addLabels` /
`removeLabels`) and state (read, starred, archived, spam). Returns the
message's labels after the change.

isSpam.description: true moves it to Spam; false recovers it.

delete.description: Sets `deleted_at`. The row stays so thread history doesn't renumber; list queries filter deleted messages out.

get.description: Returns the full RFC 5322 source as `message/rfc822`. Only available for inbound messages; outbound messages do not persist their raw source.

Streams the raw attachment bytes with the original `Content-Type` and `Content-Disposition` headers.

A PNG, JPEG, GIF or WebP is read for hidden instructions before an API key
or agent is given it, because a model can look at an image the way it reads
a body. If the text in it reads like instructions aimed at an AI, or it
cannot be checked, this returns `403 IMAGE_HELD` and a person can still open
it in the dashboard. `503 IMAGE_HELD` means it could not be checked right now
and is worth retrying. A signed-in person in the dashboard is never held, and
neither is an inbox or account that has turned mail protection off.

403.description: The image is held (`IMAGE_HELD`), or its message is quarantined (`QUARANTINED`)

503.description: The image could not be checked right now (`IMAGE_HELD`); retry shortly

post.summary: Get a short-lived download link for an attachment
post.description:
For a file too big to pass through an agent's context (a PDF as base64 is
millions of characters). Returns a link to fetch the file with a plain
`GET`, no API key. The link works for one attachment only, for 10 minutes
and 3 uses; a `HEAD` request does not spend a use. It is served as a
download, never rendered, and active types such as HTML and SVG are sent
as `application/octet-stream`. The content is untrusted: it was written
by the sender.

Refused with `403 QUARANTINED` for a message held for review, and with
`403 IMAGE_HELD` for an image whose text looks like instructions to an AI or
which could not be checked (see the attachment download). A link stops
working if its message is held after the link was issued.

url.description: Fetch with GET. The token in it is the credential.

403.description: The message is held for review (`QUARANTINED`)

404.description: No such attachment on this message

get.summary: Fetch an attachment through a download link
get.description:
The receiver for links from `download-url`. Not under `/v1` and takes no
API key: the `t` token in the query string is the credential. Every
failure, whether the token is wrong, the link expired, its uses ran out,
or the message is held, returns the same `404`, so a wrong guess learns
nothing about whether a link exists.

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: Link token

404.description: Not valid, expired, used up, or held

post.summary: Get a one-time URL to upload a file to
post.description:
For attaching a real file without putting its bytes in a request an agent
has to write out. Returns an `uploadUrl`. `PUT` the raw file to it with no
API key, then attach it by passing `{ "uploadId": "..." }` in `attachments`
on a send, reply, reply-all, forward or draft call. One file, up to 10 MB,
valid for 60 minutes, and single-use in both directions: it can be uploaded
to once and attached once.

sizeBytes.description: If known, so an oversized file is refused before upload.

put.summary: Upload a file to a one-time URL
put.description:
The receiver for URLs from `attachment-uploads`. No API key: the `t` token
in the query string is the credential. The body is the raw file bytes.
A second upload to the same URL is refused, and so is any wrong or expired
token, with the same `404`.

parameters.name: t
parameters.description: Upload token

post.description:
`labels` are applied to the message when the draft is sent. Set
`sendAt` to schedule the send: Anjal sends it at that time, no cron
needed.

400.description: Validation error, e.g. sendAt in the past, more than 90 days ahead, or a scheduled draft without recipients or a body

get.description: `scheduled=true` lists only drafts waiting to be sent, soonest first. A failed scheduled send shows `sendError`.

patch.description:
Merge-patch. Omitted fields are left as-is. Set `sendAt` to schedule or
reschedule the send (this also clears `sendError`); `sendAt: null`
cancels it.

post.description: Sends the current draft contents now and deletes the draft atomically. If the draft has `replyToMessageId`, the sent message is threaded as a reply. The draft's `labels` are applied to the sent message. Accepts an `Idempotency-Key` header.

Returns the DNS records you need to set at your registrar. Domain starts in `pending` status until you call the verify endpoint.

**Domains that already get mail elsewhere (Google Workspace, Microsoft 365).**
If the domain has MX records at another provider and you pass neither
`sharedWith` nor `replaceMailProvider`, the call returns
`422 DOMAIN_HAS_MAIL_PROVIDER` with `detectedProvider`, `mx` and a
`fix` string, because pointing the MX at Anjal would cut off that mail.
You then have three options:

1. **Keep the provider** (`sharedWith: "google" | "microsoft" | "other"`).
   No MX record is returned: the provider stays the main mail server.
   The SPF TXT record is merged into the domain's existing SPF (its
   `note` says to replace the existing record, since a domain may have
   only one). Anjal's DMARC record is only included if the domain has
   none. The response includes `routingSteps` for the provider's admin
   console: for Google, a Default routing rule that sends mail for
   non-recognized addresses to the Anjal host; for Microsoft, setting
   the Accepted domain to Internal relay plus an outbound connector to
   the Anjal smart host. In this setup the provider forwards mail for
   addresses it doesn't know, so it keeps its own users and Anjal
   receives mail only for addresses the provider doesn't have.
2. **Use a subdomain** such as `agents.example.com`, which has no MX
   yet and can point at Anjal without touching the main domain's mail.
3. **Move all mail to Anjal** (`replaceMailProvider: true`). The MX
   record returned replaces the current provider's.

sharedWith.description: Keep this provider as the domain's main mail server and add Anjal mailboxes alongside it (`shared_with` also works).

replaceMailProvider.description: Move all mail for the domain to Anjal (the returned MX record replaces the current one).

422.description: The domain already receives mail at another provider

get.description: Re-checks DNS records with the upstream ESP. If the domain is now verified, Mission Control atomically adds the new address as a primary alias on the inbox (preserving thread history). The first time this sees the domain verified, the `domain.verified` webhook fires.
Returns the current DNS records as a BIND-format zone file fragment. Convenient for pasting into a DNS editor that accepts zone-file imports.

post.description: Subscribe a URL to one or more events. See `WebhookEvent` for the full list and the newer payloads.

patch.description: Change url, events, or enabled state.

get.description: Returns counts (sent, received, bounced) and resource totals (inboxes, domains) for a time window. Workspace master keys are locked to their own workspace; tenant master keys can scope with query params.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: ISO-8601 or epoch seconds/ms. Defaults to 30 days ago.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: ISO-8601 or epoch seconds/ms. Defaults to now.

get.description:
Upgrade this GET to a WebSocket. After the handshake, the server
sends a `connected` frame and the client sends a `subscribe`
frame to start receiving events.

This protocol is wire-compatible with agentmail.to's WebSocket
API — `workspace_ids` also accepts `pod_ids` as an alias.

### Client → server frames

```json
{ "type": "subscribe",
  "event_types": ["message.received", "message.sent"],
  "inbox_ids":    ["..."],
  "workspace_ids": ["..."] }
```

### Server → client frames

```json
{ "type": "connected", "inboxId": "...", "email": "..." }
{ "type": "subscribed", "event_types": [...], "inbox_ids": [...], "workspace_ids": [...] }
{ "type": "event",
  "event_type": "message.received",
  "event_id":   "evt_...",
  "message":    { "inbox_id": "...", "thread_id": "...", "from": "...", "to": ["..."], "subject": "...", "plain_body": "...", "html_body": "...", "timestamp": "..." },
  "thread":     { "thread_id": "...", "subject": "..." } }
{ "type": "ping" }
{ "type": "error", "message": "..." }
```

Use `?api_key=<key>` as a query parameter when your client
(e.g. browser `new WebSocket`) can't set the `X-API-Key`
header.

post.description: MX-probe the recipient domain(s) to filter invalid addresses before sending. Use in combination with `verified: true` on the send endpoint.
Super admin only. Creates a new billing root and auto-provisions its Default workspace.

delete.description: Super admin only. Cascades to everything.

post.description:
Begin a LinkedIn login on behalf of the customer using their email +
password. Returns `{ ok: true, sessionId }` on direct success, or
`{ challenge: true, challengeId, challengeType }` if LinkedIn requires
a PIN (email/SMS) or mobile-app approval. Follow up with
`/sessions/verify` (PIN) or `/sessions/poll` (mobile approval).

label.description: Optional friendly label for this session.

200.description: Either a successful login or a challenge requirement.
Array of session metadata (cookies are never returned).

post.summary: Submit PIN to complete a challenge
post.description: Submit the email/SMS PIN LinkedIn sent to the customer.

For mobile-approval challenges, after the customer taps "I've approved"
in the LinkedIn mobile app. Returns 202 + `pending: true` if not yet
approved (try again in a few seconds).

Escape hatch for customers who already extracted `li_at` + `JSESSIONID`
from a logged-in browser. Skip when you can use `/sessions` instead.

Resolve a LinkedIn profile URL to its `profileId`, name, headline, and
location. Use the returned `profileId` with `/connections` for the most
reliable connection-request results.

429.description: Daily quota exceeded for this session.

post.description:
Send a LinkedIn connection request. `target` may be a profile URL
(https://www.linkedin.com/in/slug), a slug, or an `ACoA...` profileId.
Optional personalized message up to 300 characters significantly
improves acceptance rates.

target.description: Profile URL, slug, or ACoA... profileId.

429.description: Daily quota exceeded for this session.

get.description:
Lists the connected account's 1st-degree connections, newest-first.
Source for the `connection_accepted` signal kind on the cadence
runner; usable directly by clients rendering a "connections" view.

## Names are included — no profile lookup needed

Unlike the URN-only legacy LinkedIn endpoints, this response
returns fully-resolved `firstName`, `lastName`, `fullName`,
`headline`, and `pictureUrl` extracted server-side from
LinkedIn's SDUI payload. Render directly.

- `fullName`         — Convenience field, `firstName + " " + lastName`
                       with internal whitespace normalised. Use this
                       for display rather than concatenating
                       `firstName`/`lastName` yourself.
- `connectedAt`      — ISO 8601 timestamp of when the connection
                       formed. Nullable for older connections where
                       LinkedIn doesn't surface the date.
- `pictureUrl`       — Direct CDN URL. Nullable for accounts
                       without a photo. Stable enough to cache
                       for ~24h.
- `publicIdentifier` — `linkedin.com/in/<slug>` segment. Build a
                       profile URL with
                       `https://www.linkedin.com/in/${publicIdentifier}/`.
- `profileUrn`       — Use for cross-endpoint joins (matching
                       against the `participants[].urn` from
                       `GET /linkedin/conversations`, or against
                       `connection_accepted` signal payloads).

## Pagination

Newest-first. `start=0,count=50` returns the most recent 50.
LinkedIn's SDUI pager returns ~10 per page internally; this
endpoint paginates server-side to satisfy `count` up to the cap of
100. For larger backfills, page through with `start` increments.

## Worked example response

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "total": 234,
  "count": 2,
  "start": 0,
  "connections": [
    {
      "profileUrn": "urn:li:fsd_profile:ACoAAA…aaaa",
      "publicIdentifier": "jane-doe-1a2b3c",
      "firstName": "Jane",
      "lastName": "Doe",
      "fullName": "Jane Doe",
      "headline": "Head of Sales at Acme",
      "connectedAt": "2026-05-12T14:23:00Z",
      "pictureUrl": "https://media.licdn.com/dms/image/v2/…/headshot.jpg"
    },
    {
      "profileUrn": "urn:li:fsd_profile:ACoAAA…bbbb",
      "publicIdentifier": "john-smith-4d5e6f",
      "firstName": "John",
      "lastName": "Smith",
      "fullName": "John Smith",
      "headline": "Founder & CEO at Beta",
      "connectedAt": "2026-05-10T09:14:00Z",
      "pictureUrl": null
    }
  ]
}
```

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Page size. Server internally paginates LinkedIn's 10-per-page SDUI pager to satisfy this.

parameters.name: start
parameters.description: 0-based offset.

total.description: Approximate total count of 1st-degree connections (LinkedIn's count, when surfaced).

headline.description: LinkedIn's one-line tagline. May be empty string.

connectedAt.description: ISO 8601. Null for older connections where LinkedIn omits the date.

pictureUrl.description: Direct CDN URL. Null for accounts without a photo.

get.description:
Lists the connected account's outbound connection invitations that
are still pending (haven't been accepted, rejected, or withdrawn).
Drives the `connection_accepted` signal kind on the cadence runner
side; usable directly by clients rendering a "sent invitations"
view.

## Response shape — names included

Unlike older URN-only LinkedIn list endpoints, this one returns
**resolved recipient identity** already extracted server-side
from LinkedIn's SDUI payload — no follow-up `profile/lookup`
round-trip needed:

- `recipientName`              — Display name parsed from the
                                 `aria-label="Withdraw invitation
                                 sent to NAME"` anchor LinkedIn
                                 renders on each row. Always a
                                 non-empty string for valid
                                 invitations.
- `recipientPublicIdentifier`  — `linkedin.com/in/<slug>` segment.
                                 Build the profile URL as
                                 `https://www.linkedin.com/in/${slug}/`.
- `recipientUrn`               — `urn:li:fsd_profile:ACoA…`. Use
                                 when calling other LinkedIn API
                                 endpoints that take a profile URN.
- `invitationUrn`              — `urn:li:fsd_invitation:<numeric>`.
                                 Stable identifier for the
                                 invitation itself (used for
                                 withdraw on the LinkedIn side; not
                                 currently exposed as an Anjal
                                 endpoint).
- `recipientHeadline`          — Currently always empty string —
                                 the SDUI payload puts the headline
                                 in a separate textProps block we
                                 don't parse yet. Don't rely on it.
- `sentAt`                     — Currently always `null` —
                                 LinkedIn's sent-invitations SDUI
                                 page doesn't expose the original
                                 send timestamp. Don't rely on it.
- `message`                    — Currently always `null` — original
                                 invitation note isn't in the SDUI
                                 payload either. Don't rely on it.
- `state`                      — Always `"pending"` for invitations

                                 `accepted | withdrawn | rejected |

                                 reconciliation use, but the public
                                 response only ever surfaces
                                 `pending`.

- `count`  — page size, max 50, default 50

for `count > 20` may return fewer than requested; treat `total`
as advisory rather than authoritative.

## Response shape — read this before parsing

The response returns **two parallel views** of the people in each
thread:

- **`participants[]`** — preferred. Already enriched with `name`,
  `slug`, and `headline` extracted from the LinkedIn payload server-
  side, **with zero extra API calls.** Use these for rendering.
- **`participantUrns[]`** — back-compat, URN strings only.

There is **no** `participant.name` at the top level, no `peer`, no
`otherPerson`, no `lastMessage.snippet`, no `last_message` field. If
you normalise against those, every contact renders as "(unnamed)".

Field map (exact names, camelCase):

- `conversationUrn`     — `urn:li:msg_conversation:(...)`. Pass this to
                          `GET /linkedin/conversations/{conversationUrn}/messages`.
                          Always URL-encode when used as a path parameter.
- `participants[]`      — Enriched: `{ urn, name, slug, headline }`. Any
                          of name/slug/headline may be `null` (deleted
                          accounts, restricted profiles), but `urn` is
                          always present.
- `participantUrns[]`   — Mirror of `participants[].urn`. Kept for
                          back-compat with clients written before the
                          enrichment landed.
- `title`               — Group chat title only. **Null on 1-on-1
                          conversations.** Don't fall back to this for
                          the contact name; use `participants` instead.
- `lastMessage.text`    — Plain text body. Not `snippet`, not `preview`,
                          not `bodyText`.
- `lastMessage.senderName` — Display name of the sender of the latest
                          message. Already resolved server-side; null
                          only when LinkedIn omits the inline profile.
- `lastMessage.senderUrn` — URN of the same sender.
- `lastActivityAt`, `lastReadAt`, `lastMessage.deliveredAt` — Unix **ms**,
                          not seconds. Nullable for system-initiated
                          threads.

## Rendering the contact name (1-on-1 thread)

Filter your own viewer URN out of `participants`, then read `name`
directly. No profile-lookup round-trip needed:

```ts
const { conversations } = await client.linkedinListConversations({ sessionId });
const viewerUrn = (await client.linkedinGetSession({ id: sessionId })).viewerProfileUrn;

for (const c of conversations) {
  const other = c.participants.find(p => p.urn !== viewerUrn);
  const displayName = other?.name
    ?? (c.isGroup && c.title)
    ?? "(unknown)";
  // …render
}
```

participants' names with commas. For the rare case where
`participants[i].name` is null (deleted / restricted), fall back to
`POST /linkedin/profile/lookup` with the URN — but you'll only need
that on a handful of edge cases, not every conversation.

## URL-encode the path parameter

`conversationUrn` contains parens and colons — both are reserved
characters in URL paths. Always wrap in `encodeURIComponent()`
before constructing the URL:

```ts
const encoded = encodeURIComponent(conv.conversationUrn);
const r = await fetch(`/v1/linkedin/conversations/${encoded}/messages?sessionId=${sessionId}`);
```

## Response shape

Unlike `GET /linkedin/conversations`, this endpoint **does** return
`senderName` and `senderSlug` for most messages — LinkedIn embeds
the sender's display data in the message payload. They're still
nullable for system-generated messages (e.g. "X joined the
conversation"), so guard before rendering.

- `messageUrn`        — `urn:li:msg_message:(…)`. Stable identifier
                        for reaction / attachment lookups.
- `text`              — Plain text body. Empty string for attachment-

- `senderUrn`         — Profile URN. Null only on system messages.
- `senderName`        — Display name; usually `"First Last"`.

- `senderSlug`        — `linkedin.com/in/<slug>` segment. Nullable.
                        Useful when you want to build a profile URL
                        without a separate lookup.
- `isFromViewer`      — `true` when sent by the authenticated session
                        holder. Use this for left/right bubble layout.

steps (LinkedIn invite → wait → DM → email → ...) that fire
automatically per enrollment with branching on real-world events

- `leadExternalId`     — your idempotency key
- `leadName`, `leadEmail`, `leadLinkedinUrl` — whatever you sent

- `leadProfileUrn`     — `urn:li:fsd_profile:…`, set by the runner

- `sessionId`          — LinkedIn session the cadence runs through.
                           May be auto-picked from the workspace pool
                           if you didn't pass one (see commit f0d2ff1)

State + progress:

- `state`              — `active | paused | completed | replied |
                           accepted | bounced | unenrolled | error`
- `currentStep`        — 0-based index of the NEXT step due
- `stepsCompleted`     — count of DISTINCT step indices that have
                           fired with `status='sent'`. Visual: green
                           checkmark count.
- `nextStepDueAt`      — when the runner will next consider this row
                           (ISO 8601). Past time = overdue + queued.
- `lastStepFiredAt`    — ISO 8601 of the most recent step run.
- `lastError`          — most recent FAILED step run (status=
                           `failed`), or null if no failures. Keys:
                           `code`, `message`, `atStepIndex`, `firedAt`.
                           The `code` values match what `runner.ts`
                           writes — most common today are
                           `NO_SESSION_AVAILABLE`,
                           `WORKSPACE_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED`,
                           `PINNED_SESSION_UNUSABLE`, `NO_TARGET`,
                           `NO_INBOX`, `DRAFT_WEBHOOK_FAILED`
                           (your draft handler timed out, 5xx'd,
                           or returned malformed JSON), and
                           `AI_STRATEGY_REMOVED` (pre-existing
                           step still on `draftStrategy: "ai"`
                           — update the step to `static` or
                           `webhook`). Skipped steps (a step
                           whose condition didn't apply — e.g.
                           `after_accept` on a rejected invite,
                           or your draft handler returned
                           `{ skip: true }`) are NOT counted as
                           errors; they're a normal part of
                           cadence execution.

## Drilling into one enrollment

For per-step ✅ render (the full `stepRuns[]` history, including
skipped steps, rendered message text, channel URNs), call
`GET /v1/enrollments/{id}` — that endpoint returns the same
enrollment fields plus a `stepRuns` array of the last 50 runs
ordered newest-first.

post.summary: Batch-patch lead identity on multiple enrollments
post.description:
Batched form of `PATCH /v1/enrollments/{id}` for the common
recovery flow "we enrolled N leads with the wrong payload
shape; fix all of them at once."

Same merge semantics as the per-row PATCH (only fields present
in each update are touched; explicit `null` clears).

### Partial failure is allowed

A single bad row (terminal state, external-ID conflict,
not-found) does NOT fail the whole batch. The response
contains a `results[]` array mirroring the input order; each
slot is either `{ ok: true, enrollmentId, enrollment }` or
`{ ok: false, enrollmentId, code, error, detail }`. Response
status is always 200; inspect `results[i].ok` per row.

### Limits

- Max 100 updates per call. Iterate client-side for larger
  batches.
- Each `enrollmentId` must belong to the cadence in the path —
  rows pointing at a different cadence are rejected with
  `CADENCE_MISMATCH`.

### `?retryNow=true`

Applies to all rows in the batch. Same semantics as the per-row
endpoint — resets `next_step_due_at` on each successfully-
updated row to NOW so the runner re-attempts on its next tick.

### Worked example

Request:

```
POST /v1/cadences/01HY…/enrollments/bulk-relink?retryNow=true
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "updates": [
    {
      "enrollmentId": "01HZ…aaaa",
      "leadName": "Jane Doe",
      "leadLinkedinUrl": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe-1a2b3c/"
    },
    {
      "enrollmentId": "01HZ…bbbb",
      "leadName": "John Smith",
      "leadLinkedinUrl": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/john-smith/"
    }
  ]
}
```

Response:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "succeeded": 2,
  "failed": 0,
  "results": [
    { "ok": true, "enrollmentId": "01HZ…aaaa", "enrollment": { … } },
    { "ok": true, "enrollmentId": "01HZ…bbbb", "enrollment": { … } }
  ]
}
```

With one row in a terminal state:

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "succeeded": 1,
  "failed": 1,
  "results": [
    { "ok": true, "enrollmentId": "01HZ…aaaa", "enrollment": { … } },
    {
      "ok": false,
      "enrollmentId": "01HZ…bbbb",
      "code": "ENROLLMENT_TERMINAL_STATE",
      "error": "Enrollment is in terminal state 'replied'; lead identity cannot be modified.",
      "detail": { "state": "replied" }
    }
  ]
}
```

get.summary: Get an enrollment + its step-run history
get.description:
Returns the enrollment row plus its `stepRuns[]` history (last 50,
newest-first). Use this when you need per-step status — completed,
skipped, failed — to render a step-by-step ✅ timeline.

## Step run statuses

- `sent`     — step fired and LinkedIn / SMTP accepted the action.
               Render as a green checkmark.
- `skipped`  — step was evaluated but its `condition` didn't apply
               (e.g. `after_accept` step on an unaccepted invitation,
               or `never_replied` step when the lead replied).
               Normal cadence flow — render as a grey checkmark or
               skip-icon, NOT as an error.
- `failed`   — runner tried and got back `ok:false` from the
               downstream call. `errorCode` is set. The enrollment
               is deferred 1h and retried on the next tick — this
               is NOT a terminal state on its own.
- `queued`   — internal scheduling state. You'll rarely see this in
               practice; included for completeness.

## Error codes you'll see in `errorCode`

Set by `api/src/lib/cadences/runner.ts`. The catalogue:

- `NO_SESSION_AVAILABLE`      — workspace has zero connected
                                LinkedIn sessions. Customer needs
                                to connect one at /dashboard/linkedin.
- `WORKSPACE_QUOTA_EXHAUSTED` — sessions exist but all at the
                                per-action daily cap (e.g. 30
                                connection_requests/day per
                                session). Resets at midnight UTC,
                                or add more sessions.
- `PINNED_SESSION_UNUSABLE`   — `enrollment.sessionId` was set
                                manually but that session is
                                revoked / not-active / capped.
                                Customer should reconnect or
                                repin.
- `NO_TARGET`                 — `leadLinkedinUrl` (for LinkedIn
                                steps) or `leadEmail` (for email
                                steps) was missing at enrollment.
- `NO_INBOX`                  — email step but no `inboxId` on the
                                enrollment or cadence.
- `DRAFT_WEBHOOK_FAILED`      — step has `draftStrategy: "webhook"`
                                and the customer's draft handler
                                timed out (>30s), 5xx'd, returned
                                non-JSON, returned an invalid
                                defer, or returned no `body`.
                                `errorMessage` carries the upstream
                                detail (which status code, "no
                                body in response", etc). The
                                step defers 1h and retries —
                                which means a flaky handler will
                                keep getting opportunities to
                                succeed. To stop retries, mark
                                the enrollment `state: "paused"`
                                or unenroll.
- `AI_STRATEGY_REMOVED`       — pre-existing step still on
                                `draftStrategy: "ai"` (removed
                                2026-05-19). Update the step to
                                `static` (with `staticBody`) or
                                `webhook` (with the cadence's
                                `webhookUrl` set to your draft
                                handler).
- `send_failed`               — downstream LinkedIn / SMTP returned
                                an error. `errorMessage` carries the
                                upstream detail.

## Rendering ✅ progress

```ts
const r = await mam.getEnrollment({ id });
const sentByIndex = new Map<number, true>();
const skippedByIndex = new Map<number, true>();
let lastFailure: typeof r.stepRuns[number] | null = null;

for (const run of r.stepRuns) {
  if (run.status === "sent") sentByIndex.set(run.stepIndex, true);
  else if (run.status === "skipped") skippedByIndex.set(run.stepIndex, true);
  else if (run.status === "failed" && !lastFailure) lastFailure = run;
}

// For each step in cadence.steps[]:
//   if (sentByIndex.has(i))    → ✅ done
//   else if (skippedByIndex.has(i)) → ⊘ skipped (condition not met)
//   else if (i === enrollment.currentStep && lastFailure) → ⚠ blocked
//   else if (i === enrollment.currentStep) → ⏳ pending
//   else → ◯ upcoming
```

enrollment.description: Same shape as items in `/cadences/{id}/enrollments` (minus the `stepsCompleted` / `lastError` summary — drill into `stepRuns[]` below instead).

runnerState.description:
Read-only diagnostic — answers "would the runner fire this
row right now? if not, why?". Same logic the runner uses
to pick enrollments (`pickDueEnrollments` + `evaluateCondition`),
replicated read-only so callers can self-diagnose
without poking the runner.

Use this BEFORE filing a support ticket. If `pickable: true`
and the row isn't firing, the runner tick interval is 5
minutes — `maxExpectedWaitSeconds` carries the upper bound.
Use `POST /v1/cadences/{id}/run-now` to force a tick.

If `pickable: false`, `reasons[]` lists every blocking
condition with the exact PATCH curl needed to unblock.
`details` exposes the underlying values (state, scheduling,
condition evaluation) for deeper inspection.

pickable.description: True iff the runner would pick this enrollment on its next tick.

reasons.description: Empty when pickable=true. Each item is a human-readable explanation of a blocking condition, including the corrective curl when applicable.

details.description: Underlying decision inputs — state, scheduling, condition evaluation, draft strategy sanity.

maxExpectedWaitSeconds.description: Upper bound on time-to-fire when pickable=true. Null when blocked (no deterministic ETA).

stepRuns.description: Last 50 step runs for this enrollment, newest-first.

channelUrn.description: For LinkedIn steps: invitation URN / message URN / profile URN. For email: the message-id.

renderedText.description: The body that was actually sent — AI-generated or static, post-rendering.

errorCode.description: See description above for the catalogue.

skipReason.description: Why a `skipped`-status run was skipped (e.g. condition_not_met).

patch.summary: Update an enrollment (state, lead identity, scheduling)
patch.description:
Two distinct use cases — both supported by this single endpoint:

### 1. Pause / resume / unenroll

Pass `state` to move the enrollment between lifecycle states.
`active` / `paused` / `unenrolled` are the values the runner
respects. Terminal states (`completed`, `replied`, `accepted`,
`bounced`) are set by the runner itself based on signals + the
cadence's `exitOnReply` setting — don't write to them directly.

### 2. Fix-up bad enroll-time payload

Use case: a row was enrolled with the wrong shape (missing
`leadLinkedinUrl`, wrong `leadEmail`, etc.) and is now stuck on
a step with a `NO_TARGET` / `NO_INBOX` error. Patch the
identity fields and the runner picks up the corrected row on
its next tick — no need to unenroll + re-enroll (which would
lose `currentStep`, `lastStepFiredAt`, the step_runs audit, and
any `leadExternalId` joins your side has against the
enrollment).

**Merge semantics**: only fields present in the request body
are updated. Omitted fields stay as-is. Pass explicit `null` to
clear a column (where the column is nullable).

**Patchable identity fields**: `leadName`, `leadEmail`,
`leadLinkedinUrl`, `leadProfileUrn`, `leadExternalId`,
`inboxId`, `sessionId`. The runner resolves
`leadLinkedinUrl` → `leadProfileUrn` automatically when the
next LinkedIn step fires — you do not need to look up the URN
separately before patching.

### `?retryNow=true` query param

When fixing a stuck enrollment, also pass `?retryNow=true` to
reset `next_step_due_at = NOW()` so the runner re-attempts on
the next tick (~1 min) instead of waiting out the post-failure
1h backoff. Opt-in so routine patches (typo fix on a name)
don't unnecessarily trigger an immediate retry.

Successful retry automatically clears `lastError` from the
list endpoint's per-row summary — the `lastError` query
ignores failed step_runs that occurred before the most recent
successful run.

### Terminal-state guard

Patching lead identity is rejected (`409 ENROLLMENT_TERMINAL_STATE`)
when the enrollment is in `completed` / `replied` / `accepted` /
`bounced` / `unenrolled`. There's no use case for "fix a lead
on a completed cadence" — the runner won't re-run it. If you
genuinely want to resume, PATCH `state: 'active'` first, then
patch identity in a second call.

### `leadExternalId` conflict

Changing `leadExternalId` to a value another enrollment in the
same cadence already uses returns `409 LEAD_EXTERNAL_ID_CONFLICT`
with the conflicting value in the response body. The
`(cadence_id, lead_external_id)` unique constraint is what
makes the enroll endpoint idempotent — you can't violate it
via PATCH either.

### Worked example: fix-up flow

Before — list endpoint shows:

```json
{
  "id": "01HZ…",
  "leadName": null,
  "leadLinkedinUrl": null,
  "state": "active",
  "currentStep": 0,
  "stepsCompleted": 0,
  "lastError": {
    "code": "NO_TARGET",
    "message": "no_linkedin_url",
    "atStepIndex": 0,
    "firedAt": "2026-05-19T14:00:00Z"
  },
  "nextStepDueAt": "2026-05-19T15:00:00Z"
}
```

Patch request:

```
PATCH /v1/enrollments/01HZ…?retryNow=true
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "leadName": "Jane Doe",
  "leadLinkedinUrl": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe-1a2b3c/",
  "leadEmail": "jane@acme.com"
}
```

Response (immediate — `lastError` clears on the next list call
after the runner ticks successfully):

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "enrollment": {
    "id": "01HZ…",
    "leadName": "Jane Doe",
    "leadLinkedinUrl": "https://www.linkedin.com/in/jane-doe-1a2b3c/",
    "leadEmail": "jane@acme.com",
    "state": "active",
    "currentStep": 0,
    "nextStepDueAt": "2026-05-19T14:32:11Z",
    "updatedAt": "2026-05-19T14:32:11Z"
  }
}
```

parameters.name: retryNow
parameters.description:
When true, also resets `next_step_due_at = NOW()` so the
runner picks the enrollment up on the next tick instead of
waiting out the post-failure 1h backoff.

state.description: Move between lifecycle states. Terminal states are set by the runner; don't write to them.

leadName.description: Merge semantics: omit to keep, null to clear, string to set.

leadProfileUrn.description: `urn:li:fsd_profile:…`. Optional — the runner resolves this from `leadLinkedinUrl` automatically when the next LinkedIn step fires.

leadExternalId.description:
Idempotency key. Changing it to a value another
enrollment in this cadence already uses returns
409 LEAD_EXTERNAL_ID_CONFLICT.

currentStep.description:
Manual cursor advance/rewind. Use sparingly — the
runner manages this automatically. Legitimate cases:

1. Bypass an `after_accept`-gated step when the
   lead accepted out-of-band (rare).
2. Replay from a step that fired against the wrong
   inbox / session, after fixing the enrollment.
3. Abandon a step stuck on an external signal that
   won't materialise.

Range: `[0, stepCount]` inclusive. Passing
`stepCount` transitions the enrollment to
`state: completed` (`exit_reason: manually_completed`,
`next_step_due_at` cleared). Out-of-range values
return `400 STEP_OUT_OF_RANGE` with the cadence's
actual step count.

Audit: every manual advance inserts a
`linkedin_cadence_step_runs` row with
`status: skipped`,
`skip_reason: manual_advance_via_patch`, anchored to
the step the cursor was on. Visible in
`GET /v1/enrollments/{id}`'s `stepRuns[]` so anyone
auditing the cadence sees the jump.

Risk: rewinding to an earlier email step may cause
a duplicate send when the runner re-fires. LinkedIn
dedups invitations server-side; SMTP does not. Pair
with `state: paused` first if you want to inspect
before letting the runner re-fire.

200.description: Updated. Returns the full enrollment in the same shape as `GET /enrollments/{id}`'s `enrollment` field.

400.description:
`STEP_OUT_OF_RANGE` — `currentStep` was outside `[0, stepCount]`
for this cadence. Response body includes `attempted` (the value
you sent) and `stepCount` (the cadence's actual step count) so
you can correct without a follow-up GET.

404.description: Enrollment not found, or it belongs to a different tenant.

409.description:
Either `ENROLLMENT_TERMINAL_STATE` (cadence is completed/replied/
accepted/bounced/unenrolled and lead identity can't be patched
on a terminal row) or `LEAD_EXTERNAL_ID_CONFLICT` (the new
leadExternalId is already in use by another enrollment in this
cadence).

state.description: On ENROLLMENT_TERMINAL_STATE: the current state blocking the patch.

conflictingExternalId.description: On LEAD_EXTERNAL_ID_CONFLICT: the leadExternalId that's already in use.

apiKeyHeader.name: X-API-Key
apiKeyHeader.description:
Any of `sa_`, `tk_`, `wk_`, `ak_`, or `mam_` keys. Scope is enforced
per-endpoint — see individual operation descriptions.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description:
Unique value for this send (e.g. a UUID). A retry with the same key and
identical request returns the stored response (header
`Idempotent-Replayed: true`) and sends nothing. Same key with a
different request: 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED`. Same key while the
first is still running: 409 `IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS`. Blank: 400
`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_INVALID`. Keys are per account and expire after 24
hours; a failed send (non-2xx) frees the key.

LabelsQuery.name: labels
LabelsQuery.description: Comma-separated labels, e.g. `needs-review,billing`. Only results carrying every one are returned.

IncludeSpamQuery.name: includeSpam
IncludeSpamQuery.description: Spam is stored but left out by default. Pass `true` to include it (`include_spam` also works).

IdempotencyConflict.description:
`IDEMPOTENCY_KEY_REUSED` (the key was used for a different request) or
`IDEMPOTENCY_IN_PROGRESS` (the first request with this key is still running).

Labels.description:
Labels as an array or a comma-separated string. Stored lowercase and
deduplicated; at most 32 labels of at most 64 characters, no commas.

trackOpens.description:
Add a 1x1 open-tracking pixel (HTML body only; `track_opens` also
works). The stored copy never contains it. The first open fires
`message.opened`. A hint, not proof: Apple Mail Privacy Protection
prefetches images and some clients block them.

SignalKeywordMatch.description:
Fired by `kind=keyword` signals. The payload carries everything
the keyword runner already had in memory at fire time so
consumers don't need to re-scrape or re-enrich.

**Field availability:**
- `author.name|profileUrl|headline|title|companyName` —
  populated when the signal-runner's profile-cache lookup
  succeeded. `author.title` and `author.companyName` are
  parsed from the LinkedIn headline (e.g. "Founder @ Acme" →
  title="Founder", companyName="Acme").
- `author.location` — populated when profile cache had it.
- `author.followerCount` — reserved field, always null today.
  Intent is binary — a post from someone in active pain is
  valuable regardless of audience size. If your downstream
  pipeline has a real use case that needs this, tell us and
  we'll build the extractor; otherwise treat it as
  documented-for-future-expansion.
- `post.publishedAt` — best-effort absolute timestamp parsed
  from LinkedIn's relative-time string ("2h"/"3d"/"1mo"),
  precise to the minute, may drift a few minutes vs. the
  true value. Use as a recency hint, not a forensic timestamp.
- `post.engagement.{likes,comments,shares}` — reserved fields,
  always null today. Engagement count is a popularity signal,
  not an intent signal — a 0-like post from a frustrated
  founder is just as actionable as a 1000-like one. Same
  posture as followerCount: tell us if you actually need it
  and we'll build it.

**Back-compat aliases** (will stay until at least 2026-Q3):
`author.role` mirrors `author.title`; `author.company`
mirrors `author.companyName`; `post.postedAt` mirrors
`post.publishedAt`. New consumers should use the structured
names.

publishedAt.description: Absolute ISO timestamp parsed from LinkedIn's relative-time string.

postedAt.description: DEPRECATED alias of publishedAt; kept for back-compat.

engagement.description:
Post-level engagement counts. Reserved fields — always
null today. Not populated by design: engagement count
is a popularity signal, not an intent signal. If you
have a real use case that needs these, ask and we'll
build the extractor.

title.description: Parsed role from the LinkedIn headline.

companyName.description: Parsed company from the LinkedIn headline.

followerCount.description: Reserved field — always null today. Not populated by design: a post from someone in active pain is valuable regardless of audience size. Ask if you have a real use case.

engager.description: Same author-field shape as `SignalKeywordMatch.author` plus engagement-specific fields. `role`/`company` are deprecated aliases.

SignalConnectionAccepted.description:
Fired by `kind=connection_accepted` signals. No classification
block — every new connection fires by definition. The
`connection.attribution` field tells you whether this was an
acceptance of an invitation YOU sent (`outbound` — looked up
in linkedin_invitations_sent) or a cold inbound add (`inbound`).
Customers' webhook handlers can branch on this.

SignalMessageReceived.description:
Fired by `kind=message_received` signals. The runner only fires
on messages NOT sent by the viewer — your own outbound DMs are
suppressed. When a new chat's first message comes from someone
you previously sent an invitation to, the runner ALSO fans out
to any `connection_accepted` signals on the same session
(realtime acceptance shortcut).

key.description: Plain-text key — only returned on creation. Store it somewhere safe.

email.description: Current primary outbound address — may be a custom-domain alias.

canonicalEmail.description: Stable identity used for IMAP/SMTP auth. Never changes after creation.

imapPassword.description: Only returned on creation and GET /inboxes/{id}. Stored plaintext so IMAP clients can log in.

isSpam.description: Flagged by the spam filter. Spam is left out of lists unless `includeSpam=true`.

deliveryStatus.description:
Outbound only. `delivered` means the recipient's mail server
accepted it (not a guarantee of inbox placement). Null until known.

deliveredAt.description: When the recipient's mail server accepted the message (outbound only).

firstOpenedAt.description:
Time of the first open (outbound sends with `trackOpens: true`
only). NULL until the first open. Opens are a hint, not proof:
Apple Mail Privacy Protection fetches images on delivery, and
clients that block images never report an open.

lastOpenedAt.description: Most recent open event. Updates on every open.

openCount.description: Total opens. Subject to the same caveats as the timestamps.

firstClickedAt.description:
Timestamp of the first recipient link-click. Reliable signal of
engagement (unlike opens, click events are not Apple-MPP-poisoned).
NULL until the first click.

inline.description:
Present and true when `htmlBody` embedded this attachment as an inline
image and `?inlineImages=refs` replaced it with `attachment:<id>`.

labels.description: Every label carried by any message in the thread.

hasSpam.description: Present (true) only when the thread contains spam, which happens with `includeSpam=true`.

labels.description: Applied to the message when the draft is sent.

sendAt.description: When Anjal will send this draft. Null if not scheduled.

sendError.description: Why the last scheduled send failed. The draft is kept and `sendAt` is cleared.

sendAt.description:
Schedule the send: ISO 8601 with an offset, e.g.
`2026-10-01T09:00:00-04:00`. Must be in the future and at most 90
days ahead. A scheduled draft needs at least one recipient and a
body. On update, `null` cancels the schedule. Anjal checks for due
drafts about every 20 seconds. If the send fails, the draft is
kept, `sendError` is set, `sendAt` is cleared and
`draft.send_failed` fires.

WebhookEvent.description:
Payloads for the newer events:

- `message.received.spam`: inbound mail the spam filter flagged. It is
  stored but does not fire `message.received`.
- `message.sent`: includes `labels`.
- `message.delivered`: `{ messageId, inboxId, recipients, timestamp, smtpResponse }`.
  The recipient's mail server accepted it; not a guarantee of inbox placement.
- `message.rejected`: `{ messageId, inboxId, reason, recipients, timestamp }`.
  The provider refused to send it (e.g. a suppressed address).
- `message.opened`: `{ messageId, inboxId, threadId, to, subject, openedAt, userAgent }`.
  First open of a send with `trackOpens: true`. A hint, not proof.
- `draft.send_failed`: `{ draftId, inboxId, error, code }`. A scheduled
  draft could not be sent; it is kept with `sendError` set.
- `domain.verified`: `{ domainId, domain, workspaceId, sharedWith, verifiedAt }`.
  Fired when `GET /v1/domains/{domain}/verify` first sees the domain verified.

sharedWith.description:
Set when the domain's main mail stays at another provider (Google
Workspace, Microsoft 365 or other) and Anjal mailboxes live
alongside it. Null for a domain whose MX points at Anjal.

routingSteps.description:
Present only for shared domains. Steps for the provider's admin
console so it passes mail for addresses it doesn't know on to Anjal.

note.description:
Extra instructions for this record. On a shared domain the SPF
record is merged into your existing one, and the note says to
replace the existing record (a domain must have only one SPF record).

secret.description: HMAC-SHA256 secret. Only returned on creation.

kind.description:
Acquisition strategy for this signal:
  - keyword: poll LinkedIn search for the saved query.
  - engagement: poll a tracked profile/company's recent posts and fire on engagers.
  - job_change_watchlist: poll a list of profiles weekly and fire on role/company changes.

target.description: Engagement signals only — the resolved actor target.

lastSeenPostUrn.description: Engagement signals only — watermark of the most recent post processed. We only fire on engagers of posts newer than this.

watchlistCount.description: Watchlist signals only — number of profiles being tracked.

sessionId.description:
null = auto-distribute polling across all healthy LinkedIn
sessions for this tenant (recommended). Specific id = pin
the signal to that account so all polls come from it.

webhookSecret.description: Returned only on creation. Verify with HMAC-SHA256.

intentDescription.description:
Plain-English firing rule the LLM classifier uses as the
authoritative definition of what should fire. Example: "Flag as
ready when the author is a founder/operator complaining about
cold email — skip vendors, agencies, and content marketers."
The keyword is only a coarse pre-filter; this rule decides
engage=true/false and the cited reason on every match.

LinkedInSignalMatch.description:
Discriminated by `kind`. Engagement matches include `engagement.commentText` (verbatim);
job-change matches include `jobChange.{old,new}{Role,Company}`. Keyword matches leave both null.

headline.description: From the verified LinkedIn profile lookup.

role.description: Parsed current role (e.g. "Founder & CEO"). null when profile lookup was deferred.

company.description: Parsed current company. null when profile lookup was deferred.

triageScore.description: Pass-1 triage classifier score (0-100). Posts below the threshold are not persisted.

pendingEnrichment.description: true when the post passed triage but the daily profile-lookup cap forced us to skip the full Pass-2 verification. Webhook delivery is held until the next poll fully verifies the match.

sessionId.description: The LinkedIn session that actually ran the search (the router's pick when the caller didn't pin).

intentDescription.description: Plain-English firing rule used by the classifier (same semantics as on signals).

errorCode.description: Set on partial failure (e.g. LINKEDIN_RATE_LIMITED). Search row is still persisted.

rank.description: Original position in LinkedIn's ranked result list (0 = top).

counts.description: Action → count of calls in the trailing 24h. Keys: search_signal, search_history, profile_lookup, connection_request, send_message, post_like.

remaining.description: Action → remaining daily budget for this session.

delayDays.description: Days after the previous step's completion. 0 = fire on enrollment for step 0; 0.25 = 6 hours.

draftStrategy.description:
How the runner gets the rendered content for this step.

- `static`  — Use `staticBody` (+ `staticSubject` for email) as
              the message verbatim, with `{{name}}`,
              `{{first_name}}`, `{{email}}` token
              substitution. Predictable; zero external deps.
- `webhook` — At fire-time, the runner POSTs a
              `cadence.step.draft.requested` event to the
              cadence's `webhookUrl` and waits up to 30s for
              a JSON response of
              `{ body, subject?, skip?, defer? }`. The
              customer's app brings the actual content with
              its own business context, its own LLM if it
              wants one, its own thread memory. Anjal never
              generates copy on the customer's behalf.

The legacy `"ai"` value was REMOVED 2026-05-19 — Anjal no
longer drafts content server-side. New cadences passing
`"ai"` get a `VALIDATION_ERROR` with a migration hint
pointing here. Pre-existing rows with `"ai"` will surface
`AI_STRATEGY_REMOVED` as the per-enrollment `lastError.code`
when the runner tries to fire them — fix by updating the
step to `static` (with `staticBody`) or `webhook` (with the
cadence's `webhookUrl` set).

staticSubject.description: Email-only. The literal subject line for static-strategy email steps. Supports `{{name}}` / `{{first_name}}` / `{{email}}` tokens.

staticBody.description: The literal message body for static-strategy steps. Supports `{{name}}` / `{{first_name}}` / `{{email}}` tokens. Required when `draftStrategy: "static"`.

promptHint.description:
Free-text hint for the step. Anjal does not read this — it's
passed through verbatim in the `cadence.step.draft.requested`
webhook payload (`step.promptHint`) so the customer's draft
handler can use it as per-step context. Ignored by static
strategy.

notes.description: Operator notes — not sent anywhere, just stored for the customer's reference.

CadenceWebhookPayload.description:
POSTed to a cadence's `webhookUrl`. Five event types — four are
fire-and-forget notifications (you don't need to respond
meaningfully); one is a synchronous RPC.

## Fire-and-forget notifications (200 OK is fine)

| Event | When |
|---|---|
| `cadence.step.fired` | A step just ran. `result.ok` says whether it succeeded. |
| `cadence.lead.replied` | Lead replied (LinkedIn DM **or** email); enrollment transitioned to `state: replied`. `result.repliedVia ∈ {"linkedin_dm","email"}` tells you which channel. **Connection-request acceptance does not trigger this event** — that's a separate `signal.connection_accepted` webhook. `step` is `null` on this event (a reply isn't a step firing). |
| `cadence.lead.completed` | All steps fired without a reply. |
| `cadence.lead.exited` | Manual unenroll, bounce, or unrecoverable error. |

## Synchronous RPC

| Event | When | Response expected |
|---|---|---|
| `cadence.step.draft.requested` | A step with `draftStrategy: "webhook"` is about to fire — Anjal needs the content. | HTTP 200 with `{ body, subject?, skip?, defer? }` within 30 seconds. |

On a draft-request, Anjal blocks the runner waiting for your
response. Three valid response shapes:

```json
{ "body": "Hey Jane — saw your post about cold outbound...", "subject": "Re: cold outbound" }
```
Send this content. `subject` is required for email steps,
ignored for LinkedIn. `body` is the literal message text — Anjal
does NO interpretation, prompt-rendering, or LLM call on it.

```json
{ "skip": true, "reason": "lead unsubscribed in our CRM" }
```
Skip this step. The enrollment advances to the next step.
`reason` (string, max 280 chars) is stored on the step run for
audit.

```json
{ "defer": { "untilSeconds": 3600 } }
```
Reschedule. The runner sets `next_step_due_at = NOW() +
untilSeconds` and re-fires the draft request on the next tick
after that. Capped at 14 days (1209600 seconds).

Any other response (HTTP 4xx/5xx, timeout, non-JSON, missing
`body` field) fails the step with `DRAFT_WEBHOOK_FAILED`,
defers 1h, retries.

## Common headers

```
Content-Type: application/json
X-MyAgentMail-Event: cadence.step.fired | cadence.step.draft.requested
                     | cadence.lead.replied | cadence.lead.completed
                     | cadence.lead.exited
X-MyAgentMail-Signature: v1=<hex>     # HMAC-SHA256 of body using webhookSecret
User-Agent: MyAgentMail-Webhook/1.0
```

## Draft-request payload (additional fields)

Beyond the standard `cadence` / `enrollment` / `step` blocks,
draft-request includes:

- `enrollment.leadProfileUrn` — resolved by the runner from
                                `leadLinkedinUrl` after the
                                first LinkedIn step. Useful for
                                looking up the lead in your CRM.
- `enrollment.context`        — whatever JSON object you passed
                                at enrollment time, returned
                                verbatim.
- `step.promptHint`           — the customer-authored prompt
                                hint on the step. Anjal never
                                reads this — it's a pass-through
                                context channel for your handler.
- `step.condition`            — `after_accept` / `no_reply_to_prev`
                                / `never_replied` / null. Already
                                evaluated to true by the time you
                                receive the request (otherwise
                                the runner would have skipped
                                the step before drafting).
- `requestedAt`               — ISO 8601 timestamp.

## Worked example — draft handler in 30 lines

```ts
// POST /draft on your app's server
export async function handleDraft(req: Request) {
  const event = await req.json();
  if (event.type !== "cadence.step.draft.requested") return new Response("", { status: 200 });

  // Look up lead in your own CRM
  const lead = await crm.findByExternalId(event.enrollment.leadExternalId);
  if (lead.unsubscribed) {
    return Response.json({ skip: true, reason: "lead unsubscribed in CRM" });
  }

  // Generate content with YOUR LLM + YOUR business context
  const message = await yourAgent.draft({
    stepKind:  event.step.kind,
    lead,
    promptHint: event.step.promptHint,
    priorThread: await fetchPriorThread(event.enrollment.id),
    yourProduct: yourProductCatalog,
  });

  return Response.json({ body: message.body, subject: message.subject });
}
```

step.description:
Step context — present on `cadence.step.fired` and
`cadence.step.draft.requested`. `null` on
`cadence.lead.replied` (a reply isn't a step firing).

channelUrn.description: Set on cadence.step.fired for successful LinkedIn sends — the conversationUrn.

repliedVia.description:
Set on `cadence.lead.replied`. Tells you which channel
detected the reply — `linkedin_dm` for an inbound
LinkedIn message, `email` for an inbound SMTP message
whose From address matched the enrollment's leadEmail.

tags.name: LinkedIn — Signals
tags.description:
Deterministic real-time intent watchers. Every signal is a keyword
plus a plain-English firing rule (e.g. "Flag as ready when the
author is a founder complaining about cold email — skip vendors and
agencies"). Two-pass classifier:

  1. Triage — text-only LLM scores each post 0–100; obvious rejects
     drop without paying any LinkedIn quota.
  2. Verify — survivors get a profile lookup (cached, multi-session
     routed) and the full classifier runs with the author's role +
     company as authoritative context. The firing rule decides
     engage/intent, the reason cites evidence from the post.

Sessions auto-distribute — by default polling spreads across all
healthy LinkedIn sessions for the tenant, multiplying daily
throughput by the number of connected accounts. Pass a specific
sessionId on the create body to pin instead.

Optional HMAC-signed webhook delivery with automatic retries.
Auditable end-to-end.

tags.name: LinkedIn — Searches
tags.description:
Deterministic historical search across past-24h | past-week |
past-month. Synchronous — returns the full hit list inline with the
same structured output shape as signals (post + author +
classification + cited reason). The plain-English firing rule
filters to *exactly* what the buyer means; the keyword is a coarse
pre-filter. Persisted server-side so the result set can be re-opened
without spending another LinkedIn quota.
